name: Hylo Open
stakes: This week is a crucial opportunity for India's shuttlers to gain valuable ranking points and build momentum on the European circuit.
summary:
India's badminton contingent kicks off its Hylo Open campaign with a mix of high hopes and challenging openers. Top men's doubles pair Satwik & Chirag, currently ranked 6th in the world, enter the Super 500 event as the highest-ranked Indian entry and will be looking to make a deep run, though their initial draw is yet to be announced. Their consistent form makes them a formidable presence.

In the singles draws, two-time Olympic medalist PV Sindhu, ranked 8th, faces an all-Indian clash in the Round of 32 against Prakriti Bharath, a match she'll be expected to navigate. Meanwhile, Lakshya Sen, ranked 14th, has drawn Joakim Oldorff of Finland for his opening encounter, a test he'll need to overcome to build momentum. Veteran HS Prannoy and young talent Malvika Bansod are also in the fray, seeking to leave their mark. The emerging women's doubles pair of Treesa & Gayatri, ranked 17th, will aim to continue their ascent on the international stage.

With the tournament already underway, the focus will be on these early matches to see who can establish a strong foothold. The Super 500 status means valuable ranking points are on offer, making every victory crucial for India's top shuttlers.
